name: Lagan nu Custard
subtitle: the dense baked wedding custard, caramel-topped and heavy with nutmeg and cardamom
prepNotes: Reduce the milk well ahead — this is the step that takes the time, and rushing it gives a loose, watery custard.
Bring the eggs to room temperature so they blend into the warm milk without scrambling.
Preheat the oven to 160C a full 20 minutes before baking, and set a tray of hot water on the lower shelf.

steps.text: Boil the milk in a wide heavy pan and simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until reduced to about 600ml.
steps.tip: Scrape the sides back in as it reduces — those caramelised scrapings are where the flavour lives.

steps.text: Stir in the condensed milk and sugar and simmer 5 minutes more, then take off the heat and cool to lukewarm.
Beat the eggs until just smooth, with no strands of white remaining.
Pour a ladle of the warm milk into the eggs while whisking, then repeat twice before adding the eggs back into the pan.
steps.tip: Tempering is not optional. Tip cold eggs into hot milk and you get sweet scrambled egg.

steps.text: Whisk in the ground cardamom, nutmeg and rose water.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a ghee-rubbed baking dish about 25cm across.
steps.tip: Straining catches the inevitable few threads of cooked egg and is what makes the texture silky.

steps.text: Scatter the slivered almonds and pistachios over the surface.
Bake at 160C for 45 to 55 minutes, until the edges are set and the centre wobbles like a soft jelly when nudged.
steps.tip: A cracked, puffed surface means it went too far. Pull it while the middle still moves.

steps.text: If the top has not browned, run it under a hot grill for 2 minutes until patched with dark caramel spots.
Cool completely at room temperature, at least 3 hours, before cutting into squares.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days, covered. Serve chilled or at room temperature — it is never reheated, and it firms up and tastes better on the second day.
